target: Trajectory-P2-A — Real DSH Session Identity Producer (NOT implemented in H1)

integrationPoints.detail: host/dsh/lib/runner.js runWorker mints brandString(`worker-${randomUUID()}`) through agents.create and NEVER reports it on stdout, stderr or IPC
integrationPoints.verifiedIn: V0S S2 audit, re-read in H1

integrationPoints.detail: src/deployment/work_worker.ts owns the port invocation and already correlates host observations per invocation
the parent spawns `node <dshBin> --profile P --work <ctx>` with cwd=runInput.workDir and owns stdio[3]; that channel is model-unreachable, so it is the natural identity-report carrier

integrationPoints.item: the proposed narrow Session identity message shape
integrationPoints.detail: a single structured message carrying { projectId, attemptId, invocationId, dshSessionId, hostLocalJobId } on the existing channel; H1 fixes no wire format, only the consumer contract it must satisfy

integrationPoints.item: how the Parent establishes which Invocation delivered the message
integrationPoints.detail: the Parent must bind the message to the invocation it launched on THAT channel; a message on an unrelated channel is not an observation of this invocation

integrationPoints.item: fields that must be compared before accepting an observation
integrationPoints.detail: projectId, attemptId, invocationId (all exact), plus the session id the producer reports; H1 resolveVerifiedSessionBinding refuses ATTEMPT_MISMATCH and INVOCATION_MISMATCH

integrationPoints.item: facts that are ONLY Host observations
integrationPoints.detail: the session identity report is evidence of what a particular process observed; it is NOT by itself a durable canonical binding

integrationPoints.item: facts additionally required for durable binding
integrationPoints.detail: a durable, verified association record written by a designated existing owner and revalidated against canonical Attempt and Session source facts; H1 requires a non-null durableBindingRef and verification === VERIFIED
duplicates of one identity are idempotent (H1 B4); two distinct Session identities for one invocation are CONFLICTING_SESSION_IDENTITY (H1 B5); a marked conflict is refused before any resolution

integrationPoints.item: failure windows before and after IPC delivery
integrationPoints.detail: before delivery the Parent has no identity report (NO_ASSOCIATION_EVIDENCE); after delivery but before a durable association it has an observation only (DURABLE_BINDING_MISSING) — neither establishes BOUND_VERIFIED

integrationPoints.item: how a cold restart changes what can be proven
integrationPoints.detail: a SessionId that remains present does not restore Attempt ownership; only a durable association survives (H1 B7). Cold recovery of the association itself is P2-B and is NOT tested in H1.

integrationPoints.item: how H1 contracts will be consumed
integrationPoints.detail: H1 page integrity validates the page a producer-supplied session yields; H1 verified binding resolution supplies the session id to read. P2-A success alone must NOT be called BOUND_VERIFIED unless the source and durability requirements actually hold.

stages.P2-B: Durable Attempt→Invocation→Session binding and cold recovery
stages.P2-C: Real attributed Execution Trajectory and Handoff Preview

readyToBegin: P2-A is READY to begin: the consumer-side contract is fixed and typed, the resolver refuses every insufficient evidence class, and the ordinary Preview remains zero-read and incapable of elevating a claim. The producer itself is NOT implemented.
